q1.prompt: On a sorted array you need two numbers that sum to a target. Which method?

choices.label: Two pointers at the ends — move the end that shrinks the gap

wrong_nested.explanation: On a sorted array, opposite-end pointers move in O(n). Nested pairs work but waste the sorted order.

q2.prompt: Which missing property breaks the two-pointer argument?

choices.label: As a substitute for a hash map on unsorted two-sum when you cannot sort

wrong_refuse.prompt: Unsorted two-sum needs a map if you cannot sort.
wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid two pointers as a substitute for a hash map on unsorted two-sum when you are not allowed to sort. Avoid moving both pointers every iteration without an invariant.

success.prompt: You used end pointers on sorted sums and avoided them when hashing fits better.
